title: Computation of unbounded derived morphisms on arbitrary K-injective resolutions
statement:
Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B$ be abelian categories [def-sp-abelian] and $F:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ an additive functor [def-sp-left-exact-additive]. Write $K(\mathcal A)$ for complexes modulo chain homotopy and $Q_{\mathcal A}:K(\mathcal A)\to D(\mathcal A)$ for localization at quasi-isomorphisms [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and similarly for $\mathcal B$. Assume every complex of $\mathcal A$ has a K-injective resolution, meaning a quasi-isomorphism to a complex $I$ with $\operatorname{Hom}_{K(\mathcal A)}(E,I)=0$ for every acyclic $E$. Let $(RF,\eta)$ be the unbounded total right derived functor [def-sfb-right-derived-functor], with unit $\eta_N:Q_{\mathcal B}(FN)\to RF(Q_{\mathcal A}N)$. For a K-injective resolution $a:N\to I$, set
$$c_a=\eta_I^{-1}\circ RF(Q_{\mathcal A}a):RF(Q_{\mathcal A}N)\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_{\mathcal B}(FI).$$
For complexes $N,N'$, any morphism $h:Q_{\mathcal A}N\to Q_{\mathcal A}N'$ in the derived category, and K-injective resolutions $a:N\to I$, $b:N'\to J$, there is a unique homotopy class $g:I\to J$ with
$$Q_{\mathcal A}g=(Q_{\mathcal A}b)\circ h\circ(Q_{\mathcal A}a)^{-1},$$
and
$$c_b\circ RF(h)\circ c_a^{-1}=Q_{\mathcal B}(Fg).$$
Here $Fg$ means degreewise application of $F$ to any representative of that homotopy class. These formulas are compatible with identities and composition of derived morphisms. For another resolution $a':N\to I'$, the canonical transition $c_{a'}c_a^{-1}$ is $Q_{\mathcal B}(Fk)$ for the unique homotopy class $k:I\to I'$ satisfying $Q_{\mathcal A}k=Q_{\mathcal A}a'(Q_{\mathcal A}a)^{-1}$; these transitions are isomorphisms, satisfy the cocycle identity for three resolutions, and intertwine the displayed formula for every $h$.
